title: Mirror code before PackNet physical allocation
hypothesis: For task updates that lie near a shared functional-view basis, trying a compact View before allocating per-task PackNet weights reduces stored physical values and bytes; novel residuals should trigger private allocation without harming earlier tasks.
physical_object: shared 128-coordinate task basis embedded in D=2048 fixed mask/weight space
mirror_coordinate: three coefficients over shared basis; sparse private residual on split
logical_multiplicity: 12 sequential linear task functions: eight shared-view tasks then four novel tasks
controls: PackNet-style independent sparse task weights and indices
Mirror shared basis plus codes and private residual fallback
generic rank-3 PCA on support discovered from the first eight tasks, with the same sparse residual fallback
generic robust shared basis inferred from first eight tasks, with sparse outlier fit and private residual fallback

development.selection_metric: actual serialized bytes, query NRMSE, private allocation count

paid_objects: PackNet task indices and fp16 values
PCA shared-support indices, mean, basis and codes
private residual int16 indices and fp16 values
generic shared basis indices, basis, codes and residuals

success_gate: At query NRMSE <=0.05, Mirror with private fallback uses at least 30% fewer private values and bytes than PackNet independent storage, and triggers private allocation for novel tasks while retaining the first eight tasks.
failure_gate: Shared View misses quality on novel tasks and fallback fails to recover it, or Mirror does not reduce allocation/bytes; generic PCA matching means no Mirror-specific result. Robust shared-basis control matching Mirror means no Mirror-specific result.
boundaries: PackNet is approximated as independent sparse task weights; no iterative pruning/training
Task family contains constructed shared and novel components
Retention measured as simultaneous reconstruction, not sequential optimizer retention
